subject: chemistry

moments.title: Liebig's combustion analysis
moments.body: Liebig perfects combustion analysis — burning an organic compound to determine its C, H, O content. He sets up the first modern teaching laboratory at Giessen and trains a generation of chemists.
moments.takeaway: Quantitative organic chemistry — and the first chemistry teaching lab — emerge.

moments.title: Liebig's mineral fertiliser
moments.body: Liebig proves plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK), not 'humus'. He launches the artificial fertiliser industry.
moments.takeaway: Modern agriculture begins with a chemist's analysis of plant ash.

moments.title: Liebig's Extract of Meat
moments.body: Liebig commercialises a beef-extract product, predecessor to OXO and stock cubes. He also gives his name to the Liebig condenser, still standard in every chemistry lab.
moments.takeaway: A chemist becomes a household name through fertilisers and stock cubes.

moments.title: NPK feeds the world
moments.body: Roughly 200 Mt of N fertiliser per year (mainly Haber-Bosch) feeds half of humanity. NPK runoff also drives ocean dead zones.
moments.takeaway: Liebig's fertilisers feed the planet — and pollute it.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Precision agriculture, slow-release fertilisers and microbial-based N fixation are major research areas to reduce fertiliser overuse.
now.open_questions: Can we replace synthetic fertilisers with biological N-fixation?

reflection: Liebig's fertilisers saved billions from hunger and damaged the global nitrogen cycle. Are some inventions both irreversibly good and bad?
